title: A travelling-wave strategy for plant–fungal trade
abstract: For nearly 450 million years, mycorrhizal fungi have constructed networks to collect and trade nutrient resources with plant roots. Owing to their dependence on host-derived carbon, these fungi face conflicting trade-offs in building networks that balance construction costs against geographical coverage and long-distance resource transport to and from roots. Here we built a custom-designed robot for high-throughput time-lapse imaging tracking over 500,000 fungal nodes and ~100,000 cytoplasmic flow trajectories, and found that mycorrhizal fungi build networks as self-regulating travelling waves — pulses of growing tips pull an expanding wave of nutrient-absorbing mycelium whose density is self-regulated by fusion.
